tagline: A multi-brand direct selling company in home organization and beauty transforming lives through entrepreneurship
hero_kpi_rationale: The high and expanding gross margin reflects the strength of the asset-light business model and the successful integration of Jafra, a key profitability driver despite revenue volatility. A reclassification in 2024 adjusted margins for prior periods to properly reflect production costs.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue that remains after deducting direct production and distribution costs.
kpis.description: The adjusted gross margin for 2024 incorporates the reclassification of production costs initially misclassified. For 2023 (restated data), the margin was 67.2%, corrected for the reclassification of 559.6 M MXN in direct costs.
kpis.signal: Stabilization of gross margin following production cost corrections in 2024.

kpis.name: EBITDA Margin
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization divided by revenue.
kpis.description: EBITDA margin stands at 17.6% in 2024, reflecting the operational transition post-Jafra acquisition and integration costs.
kpis.signal: Slight compression of EBITDA margin due to Jafra integration and financing costs.

kpis.name: Net Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total sales after deductions, returns, and discounts.
kpis.description: Consolidated net revenue reached 14.8 Bn MXN in 2024, growing 13.6% compared to 2023 (13.0 Bn MXN), with Jafra contributing 57.5% of the total and Betterware 42.5%.
kpis.signal: Measured growth driven by Jafra (57.5% of total in 2024) and Betterware (42.5%).

kpis.name: Free Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated from operations after investments.
kpis.description: Estimated FCF for 2024 reaches approximately 1150 M MXN, reflecting significant improvement compared to 2023 (678.8 M MXN), driven by operational normalization post-acquisition.
kpis.signal: Strong cash generation in 2024, despite debt and interest burden.

kpis.name: Net Debt / EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Leverage ratio measuring the ability to repay debt.
kpis.description: The trailing 12-month net debt / EBITDA ratio is 2.1x in 2024, down from 2.3x in Q1 2023 and 2.6x in Q4 2022. The reduction of long-term debt balance by approximately 1.0 Bn MXN in 2023 confirms the deleveraging trajectory.
kpis.signal: Gradual improvement in leverage through operational cash flow generation, targeting a range of 1.5x to 2.0x.

kpis.name: Headcount (employees)
kpis.explanation: Total number of direct employees in the group (excluding consultants / independent distributors).
kpis.description: The company employs approximately 1,800 people in 2024, primarily supporting distribution and administration. The majority of the sales network relies on 10+ levels of Jafra consultants and independent Betterware distributors.
kpis.signal: Moderate headcount growth consistent with a direct selling model based on consultants and independent distributors.

kpis.name: Sales CAGR 2019-2022
kpis.explanation: Compound annual growth rate of sales over the 2019-2022 period, prior to the major Jafra acquisition.
kpis.description: Betterware achieved an organic CAGR of 24% between 2019 and 2022 at the standalone Betterware group level (pre-Jafra), demonstrating the momentum in the Mexican home organization market.
kpis.signal: Strong organic growth prior to the April 2022 acquisition of Jafra.

kpis.name: EBITDA CAGR 2019-2022
kpis.explanation: Compound annual growth rate of adjusted operating profit over 2019-2022 (pre-Jafra acquisition).
kpis.description: Betterware group's EBITDA CAGR between 2019 and 2022 was 31%, showing strong profitability improvement driven by economies of scale and enhanced operational efficiency.
kpis.signal: Progressive improvement in operational profitability before Jafra integration.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions.
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends + buybacks (2021-2025) in billions USD. Source yfinance cashflow.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du résultat net redistribuée. >80 % = potentiellement non soutenable.

risks.title: Dependence on independent distributors
risks.score_rationale: Central position in Item 1A, strong language ("direct dependence", "high turnover"), stable trend, high weight due to linkage with core business model.

risks.title: Loss of top-level distributors
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in risks, concerned language ("negatively impact"), stable trend, high weight as these actors generate a significant share of sales.

risks.title: Dependence on manufacturers in China
risks.score_rationale: Clearly highlighted in text, warning language ("could harm"), stable trend, high weight due to logistical and geopolitical risks.

risks.title: Regulation of direct selling in Mexico
risks.score_rationale: Present in Mexico-related risks, serious tone ("may restrict", "affect profitability"), stable trend, significant weight in an emerging regulatory context.

risks.title: Risk of reclassification of distributors
risks.score_rationale: Highly prominent, strong language ("could result in significant liability"), stable trend, very high weight due to potential financial consequences.

risks.title: Cybersecurity of information systems
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in technology risks, preventive but serious language, stable trend, increasing weight with digitalization.

risks.title: Increased competition in the local market
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly cited, warning language ("material adverse effect"), stable trend, high weight due to pressure on market share.

risks.title: Interruption of the Querétaro site
risks.score_rationale: Specific operational risk, strong language ("material effect"), stable trend, high weight for the beauty and personal care segment.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or related technologies in the provided documents. The company does not appear to position AI as a strategic lever. Mentioned innovations relate to mobile applications (Jafranet 2.0) and e-commerce tools without AI integration.
evidence: No reference to AI, machine learning, or AI-based automation tools.
Mentioned mobile innovations (Jafranet 2.0) do not explicitly use AI.
No indication of R&D investment specific to AI or emerging technologies.
